records.summary: Wake an agent to resolve a failed critical function, with the structured data attached. The estate's session door (sb start) is tried first -- it is the sanctioned fleet-scale work plane, with its budget, its approval gates and its runner registry -- and the local claude lane is the fallback, because the session door is down at the moment (Temporal unreachable; nothing listens on 127.0.0.1:16223). Which lane was used is returned in the result, because a claim of "an agent was invoked" that does not say how is not a claim. The task is free text, and it is what the woken agent is told to do; put the measurements, the paths and the constraint in it ("measure what you changed; do not touch another agent's worktrees"). The incident is optional and is appended to the prompt verbatim. class: mutate args: task: {type: string, default: "", description: "what the woken agent must do"} incident: {type: string, default: "", description: "optional JSON incident record, appended verbatim"} runner: {type: string, default: "claude", description: "the session plane's runner registry name"} repo: {type: string, default: "", description: "the repository the agent works in"} budget: {type: int, default: 20, description: "the session plane's budget"} door_s: 90 halt_on_failure: false steps: - name: invoke on_fail: continue cmd: | # The payload is built from the ENVIRONMENT, not from quoted template text: interpolate() # already quotes, so a second pair of quotes around an empty value is literal text (the # 2026-10-18 shape that made site-onboard dead at every door), and a task that contains a # quote or a newline survives this way and cannot break the command. TASK={{task}} INCIDENT={{incident}} RUNNER={{runner}} REPO={{repo}} BUDGET={{budget}} \ python3 -c 'import json,os; print(json.dumps({"task": os.environ.get("TASK",""), "incident": json.loads(os.environ.get("INCIDENT") or "{}"), "runner": os.environ.get("RUNNER","claude"), "repo": os.environ.get("REPO",""), "budget": int(os.environ.get("BUDGET") or "20")}))' \ > ~/.estate/agent-invoke.payload.json bash ~/.estate/libexec/agent-invoke.sh --task-file ~/.estate/agent-invoke.payload.json echo $? > ~/.estate/agent-invoke.rc - name: verdict cmd: | rc=$(cat ~/.estate/agent-invoke.rc 2>/dev/null || echo 1) case "$rc" in 0) echo "verdict: an agent was invoked; the lane it used is in the line above" ;; 3) echo "verdict: no agent could be invoked (no session door and no local claude lane)" ;; *) echo "verdict: the invocation door could not run (rc=$rc)" ;; esac exit "$rc

Uses bin/build-image from the idp repo (R24 enforced there). args: image: { type: string, help: "Image name, e.g. fleetview-backend" } ref:   { type: string, default: "main", help: "Git ref to build" } tools: [bash, git, docker] models: [] halt_on_failure: true max_turns: 5 steps: - cmd: > ~/Documents/code/idp/bin/build-image {{image}} {{ref}} on_fail: halt

Make the estate bus beside the door answer, or say why it cannot. Probes the NATS protocol on loopback (a socket that opens but never sends INFO is silent, not alive), and if nothing answers starts the broker detached from any job's process group. A broker is never started twice: the probe runs first and an answering broker is left alone. Exit 0 when the bus answers, 1 when it stays silent, 2 when it cannot even try. class: mutate args: port: {type: int, default: 4222} halt_on_failure: true steps: - name: bus-ensure cmd: > bash ~/.estate/libexec/bus-ensure.sh

Composite intent. API server health, etcd latency, scheduler latency. Returns structured output via metrics apiserver_request_duration_seconds. args: kubeconfig: {type: string, default: ""} steps: - name: apiserver-health cmd: > KUBECONFIG={{kubeconfig}} kubectl --request-timeout=30s get --raw /healthz 2>/dev/null - name: etcd-health cmd: > KUBECONFIG={{kubeconfig}} kubectl --request-timeout=30s get --raw /healthz/etcd 2>/dev/null - name: apiserver-latency cmd: | KUBECONFIG={{kubeconfig}} kubectl --request-timeout=30s get --raw /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('\n'.join(f\"{n['metadata']['name']}: cpu={n.get('usage',{}).get('cpu','0')} mem={n.get('usage',{}).get('memory','0')}\" for n in d.get('items',[])[:3]) or 'no metrics')

Composite intent. Warning events since timestamp. Default 1h. args: since:     {type: string, default: "1h"} namespace: {type: string, default: ""} kubeconfig: {type: string, default: ""} steps: - name: events cmd: | # `-n ""` is not a valid kubectl flag, so an empty namespace means every namespace. # `get events` no longer accepts --field-selector/--sort-by (kubectl routes it to the # `events` verb), so the Warning filter and the ordering happen here. # NO SHELL QUOTES AROUND A TEMPLATE: interpolate() already quotes the value, so `ns=''` # is an empty value (the 2026-10-18 shape that made site-onboard dead at every door). ns={{namespace}} if [ -n "$ns" ]; then nsflag="-n $ns"; else nsflag=-A; fi KUBECONFIG={{kubeconfig}} kubectl --request-timeout=30s \ $nsflag get events -o json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c " import json, sys evs = [e for e in json.load(sys.stdin).get('items', []) if e.get('type') == 'Warning'] evs.sort(key=lambda e: e.get('lastTimestamp') or '') print(f'{len(evs)} warning events:') for e in evs[-20:]: obj = e.get('involvedObject', {}) msg = e.get('message', '')[:80] print(f\"  {e.get('lastTimestamp', '')} {obj.get('kind')}/{obj.get('name')} — {msg}\")

Composite intent. Nodes + problem pods (restarts/crashloop) + warning events. Use namespace= to scope to one namespace. args: namespace: {type: string, default: ""} since:     {type: string, default: "1h"} steps: - name: nodes intent: kubectl args: resource: nodes output: wide - name: problem-pods intent: kubectl-list args: resource: pods namespace: "{{namespace}}" field: status.phase!=Running output: wide - name: warning-events intent: kubectl args: resource: events output: wide extra: --all-namespaces --field-selector type=Warning --sort-by='.lastTimestamp

Composite intent. CSI driver issues + unbound/pending PVCs. args: kubeconfig: {type: string, default: ""} steps: - name: csi-drivers cmd: | KUBECONFIG={{kubeconfig}} kubectl --request-timeout=30s \ get csidrivers -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.metadata.annotations.storage\.kubernetes\.io\/createdby}{"\n"}{end}' - name: pending-pvcs intent: kubectl-list args: resource: pvc all_ns: true output: json - name: storage-usage cmd: | KUBECONFIG={{kubeconfig}} kubectl --request-timeout=30s \ get persistentvolumeclaims -A -o json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c " import json, sys items = json.load(sys.stdin).get('items', []) pending = [p for p in items if p['status']['phase'] not in ('Bound', 'Deleted')] bound = [p for p in items if p['status']['phase'] == 'Bound'] print(f'Total: {len(items)} | Bound: {len(bound)} | Pending: {len(pending)}') for p in pending[:5]: print(f\"  {p['metadata']['namespace']}/{p['metadata']['name']} — {p['status'].get('phase', '?')}\")

Run the full 4-tier code review pipeline on a diff or files. Tier 0 (deterministic) always runs. Tier 2 (LLM) only runs on Tier 0+1 output. Tier 3 verifies every Tier 2 finding before surfacing. Stochastic judgment proposes; deterministic verification disposes. args: target:    {type: string, default: "",   help: "File, dir, or git ref to review."} since:     {type: string, default: "HEAD~1", help: "Git ref for diff base."} tier:      {type: string, default: "all",    help: "0|1|2|3|all. Run only selected tiers."} severity:  {type: string, default: "medium", help: "low|medium|high|critical. Minimum severity."} halt_on_failure: false steps: # The tiers hand off through files, not env: each step is its own shell, so a # variable set in one step is gone in the next. Without this the pipeline ran # Tier 0 and Tier 1 and then had nothing to judge (2026-10-26). - name: t0 cmd: > mkdir -p $HOME/.estate/review/latest && python3 ~/.estate/libexec/code-review-t0.py {{tier}} {{target}} {{since}} | tee $HOME/.estate/review/latest/t0.json - name: t1 cmd: > mkdir -p $HOME/.estate/review/latest && python3 ~/.estate/libexec/code-review-t1.py {{tier}} {{target}} {{since}} | tee $HOME/.estate/review/latest/t1.json - name: t2 cmd: > mkdir -p $HOME/.estate/review/latest && python3 ~/.estate/libexec/code-review-t2.py {{tier}} {{target}} {{since}} | tee $HOME/.estate/review/latest/t2.json - name: t3 cmd: > mkdir -p $HOME/.estate/review/latest && python3 ~/.estate/libexec/code-review-t3.py {{tier}} {{target}} {{since}} | tee $HOME/.estate/review/latest/t3.json

The estate-wide critical-function spine. It reads catalog/critical-functions.json -- the one declarative registry of the functions the estate cannot work without -- and measures each one: LIVENESS (is it running: a heartbeat file, a socket, a port, an HTTP endpoint, a launchd job, a command, a file) and, where one is declared, its GOAL (is it doing its job: free space on a volume, a numeric field in a heartbeat). A function that is ALIVE and missing its goal is FAILING, which is the case the old disk watcher was: running, ticking, freeing nothing. Verdicts are PASS, FAIL and BLIND. BLIND is a verdict, not a quiet PASS: a probe that cannot be measured proves nothing, and reporting it as PASS is how a gate stops being a gate. A failure raises a structured incident (~/.estate/incidents/<id>.json, a ledger, and latest.json), alerts (a macOS notification and ~/.estate/alerts/inbox.jsonl), and wakes an agent to resolve it with the structured data attached -- through the estate's session door when it is up, and through the local claude lane when it is not, always recording which lane was used. Alerts and invocations are deduplicated and backed off (300s, 600s, 1200s, 1800s), so a function that stays dead does not spawn an agent storm. Exit 0: every function PASSes. Exit 1: at least one FAILs. Exit 2: at least one is BLIND and none FAILs. dry_run=1 measures and reports without raising anything. class: mutate args: registry: {type: string, default: "", description: "path to the registry; the runtime tree's catalog/ by default"} only: {type: string, default: "", description: "check one function id"} dry_run: {type: int, default: 0, description: "1 = measure and report only; raise nothing"} door_s: 90 halt_on_failure: false steps: - name: check on_fail: continue cmd: | REG="" [ -n {{registry}} ] && REG="--registry {{registry}}" ONLY="" [ -n {{only}} ] && ONLY="--only {{only}}" DRY="" [ "{{dry_run}}" = "1" ] && DRY="--dry-run" python3 ~/.estate/libexec/critical-watch.py --json $REG $ONLY $DRY echo $? > ~/.estate/critical-watch.rc - name: verdict cmd: | rc=$(cat ~/.estate/critical-watch.rc 2>/dev/null || echo 1) case "$rc" in 0) echo "verdict: every critical function passes" ;; 1) echo "verdict: at least one critical function FAILED -- the incident, the alert and the agent are in ~/.estate/incidents/" ;; 2) echo "verdict: at least one critical function is BLIND (the probe could not be measured)" ;; *) echo "verdict: the spine could not run (rc=$rc)" ;; esac exit "$rc
Crystallize an ephemeral pattern into a durable intent YAML. topic= command= description= dry_run=true force=false.

Artifact policy routes work; a test decides. verb=plan|dispatch|status spec=<md> slug=<name> repo= planner=auto builder=auto reasoning=standard risk=standard parallel=3 max_turns=30 attempts=3. Ordinary planning is mid-tier; deep/high-risk work is frontier; two gated failures trigger frontier re-planning. Explicit model names are manual overrides.

Free the laptop's data volume by deleting ONLY regenerable weight. Dry run by default: every target with its measured size. apply=true deletes the allow-list and nothing else, then proves it: each target must be gone (exit 3 if not), and the free space before and after is measured, not estimated. The allow-list is package-manager caches (yarn berry, go-build, pip, Homebrew, npm/npx, uv), the estate's own temp scratch (including the pytest scratch every local gate run leaves behind), and the Cargo target/ dirs of the idp main checkout. Under a floor it also reclaims re-installable toolchain weight: superseded node versions, old rustup toolchains, superseded claude-code builds, and the estate's own global npm packages that nothing in the estate runs -- keeping the newest of each family, any version the estate's own runtime names, anything a running process holds open, and rustup's default toolchain. THE ESTATE'S TOOL CACHE IS NEVER RECLAIMED (measured 2026-10-28). It looked like 1330M of regenerable tooling, and reclaiming it deleted kyverno, helm, kustomize, kubeconform, flux, conftest, temporal and the gate's own python -- so the estate's own gate then reported "helm or kyverno CLI not installed". A tool the estate's own doors use is not reclaimable weight. THE ORDER IS THE ENGINE'S, and there is only one: caches, then the toolchain tier, then docker, then worktrees, then temp, then the Chrome clones, then the report. The toolchain tier is SECOND because it is the only tier with real weight (2.2G measured) and because the phases after it are slow and usually yield nothing (a worktree is another agent's checkout; the container engine is not answering). Nothing is reclaimed past the target: the run stops the moment the volume is back above it. target_mb=N is that target (0 = no target). The executor's own floor is 1500 MB (MIN_FREE_MB in mcp/plugins/estate_executor.py) and it refuses to start a job below it, so a target at or above it is what keeps the estate's doors working. incremental=1 is the resident guardian's mode: the fast tiers only -- caches, the toolchain tier and the temp scratch -- with no HOME scan, no worktree walk and no docker probe. Every step is idempotent, so a step that did not finish is the next step's work. only_below_mb=N applies only while free space is under N MB. trash=true also empties ~/.Trash (the user's; opt-in only). worktrees=true also removes settled agent worktrees: clean, every commit on a branch/tag/remote, unlocked, idle 6h, no process inside, via `git worktree remove` without --force (restorable with `git worktree add`). A delete is bounded (DELETE_S, 30s) and resumable: rm of what is left continues where it stopped, so a run that is cut short says so and the work is still owed (exit 4) rather than failing. Exit 5 means another run holds the lock and is doing the work: that is not a failure, and the verdict prints the measured free space. class: mutate args: apply: {type: bool, default: false} trash: {type: bool, default: false} only_below_mb: {type: int, default: 0} worktrees: {type: bool, default: false} budget_s: {type: int, default: 78, description: "seconds of work the cleaner may start; keep under door_s"} target_mb: {type: int, default: 0, description: "keep reclaiming until this much is free; 0 = no target"} incremental: {type: int, default: 0, description: "guardian mode: the fast tiers only, no HOME scan"} # 95, and it used to declare nothing at all, so it inherited the ceiling: the dry run's du of HOME # (T_SCAN 300s) then hit the door at 100s and reported a timeout with no measurement in it. door_s: 95 halt_on_failure: true steps: - name: run # The cleaner's own status is carried out of the step, so the verdict below can say what # happened in one line -- including the case that is not a failure (5: another run holds the # lock and is doing the work). on_fail: continue cmd: | env DISK_CLEANUP_TARGET_MB={{target_mb}} DISK_CLEANUP_INCREMENTAL={{incremental}} \ bash ~/.estate/libexec/disk-cleanup.sh {{apply}} {{trash}} {{only_below_mb}} {{worktrees}} {{budget_s}} echo $? > ~/.estate/disk-cleanup.rc - name: verdict cmd: | rc=$(cat ~/.estate/disk-cleanup.rc 2>/dev/null || echo 1) case "$rc" in 0) echo "verdict: the cleaner ran" ;; 5) echo "verdict: another run holds the lock and is doing the work (the measured free space is above)"; rc=0 ;; 4) echo "verdict: the budget ran out with work still owed -- the resident guardian carries it, or run this door again" ;; 3) echo "verdict: a target survived deletion (see the lines above)" ;; *) echo "verdict: the cleaner could not run (rc=$rc)" ;; esac exit "$rc

Free space now, inside the door's 100s, by running the estate's own cleaner (platform/estate/libexec/disk-cleanup.sh) in apply mode under a budget it can finish. It deletes ONLY what the cleaner already allows -- package-manager caches, dangling images and build cache, settled agent worktrees it archives first, stale temp (including the pytest scratch every local gate run leaves behind), leftover Chrome code-sign clones, and (under its floor) re-installable toolchain weight -- and widens nothing. The estate's own tool cache is not weight: it holds the gate's python, kyverno, helm and the rest, and reclaiming it takes the estate's own doors down with it. worktrees=true by default because that is where the gigabytes are. ONE ORDER, AND IT IS THE ENGINE'S: caches, then the toolchain tier, then docker, then worktrees, then temp, then the Chrome clones. The toolchain tier is second because it is the only tier with real weight and the phases after it are slow and usually yield nothing; the door used to ask for the toolchain tier "first", which selected it but did not reorder it, so the worktree walk ran in front of the 2.2G and the door spent its budget there. Now one call, in the engine's order, spends the budget where the bytes are. Every phase either runs inside what is left of the budget or is SKIPPED BY NAME with the seconds it was denied, and free space is reported before and after, measured. A delete is bounded (30s) and resumable, so a run that is cut short says the work is still owed instead of failing. Exit 4 means work remains: the resident guardian (ai.estate.disk-watch) carries it, or run this door again -- every phase is idempotent. The RESIDENT GUARDIAN is the estate's continuous answer; this door is the on-demand sweep. Use when bin/idp-disk-guard says the volume is under the door's floor. class: mutate args: worktrees: {type: bool, default: true, description: "also remove settled agent worktrees (archived first)"} trash: {type: bool, default: false, description: "also empty ~/.Trash (the user's; opt-in)"} target_mb: {type: int, default: 0, description: "keep reclaiming until this much is free; 0 = no target"} # 95, not 100: the steps around the cleaning call need a few seconds, and a door that declares # exactly the ceiling spends its last second being killed. door_s: 95 halt_on_failure: false steps: - name: before cmd: | df -k /System/Volumes/Data | awk 'NR==2 {printf "free before: %dM on %s\n", $4/1024, $9}' - name: clean # One call, in the engine's order, with a budget it can finish inside the door. The cleaner's # own status is carried out of the step: 0 every phase ran, 4 work still owed, 3 something # that should be gone is still there, 5 another run holds the lock and is doing the work. on_fail: continue cmd: | env DISK_CLEANUP_TARGET_MB={{target_mb}} \ bash ~/.estate/libexec/disk-cleanup.sh true {{trash}} 0 {{worktrees}} 78 echo $? > ~/.estate/disk-free.rc - name: after on_fail: continue cmd: | df -k /System/Volumes/Data | awk 'NR==2 {printf "free after: %dM on %s\n", $4/1024, $9}' - name: verdict cmd: | rc=$(cat ~/.estate/disk-free.rc 2>/dev/null || echo 1) case "$rc" in 0) echo "verdict: every phase ran" ;; 4) echo "verdict: the budget was spent with work still owed -- the guardian continues it, or run disk-free again" ;; 5) echo "verdict: another run holds the lock and is doing the work (the measured free space is above)"; rc=0 ;; 3) echo "verdict: a target survived deletion (see the lines above)" ;; *) echo "verdict: the cleaner could not run (rc=$rc)" ;; esac exit "$rc

Reclaim the data volume when the executor's floor refuses every door (measured 2026-10-28: 426 MB free, floor 1500 MB, so every estate_execute and every git MCP tool refused while the machine was starved). Two actions, both narrow and both measured: 1. stop the local gate runs this machine is running TWICE. bin/idp-ci is a full sweep and two of them at once on a 113 GiB volume is what emptied it; the estate's real gate is the one GitHub Actions runs on the branch, so a duplicate LOCAL sweep is stopped rather than left to starve every other agent. Only the pids named by the caller are signalled, and only when their command line is the gate itself. 2. delete the pytest scratch directories of runs that FINISHED: pytest-of-* directories older than the age given, with no process holding anything open inside them (lsof decides, not the timestamp). A live test's scratch is never touched. 3. (added 2026-10-28) reclaim the ESTATE'S OWN regenerable weight, which no other door covers: the executor's per-job run records under ~/.estate/runs (one .log/.pid/.exit per job -- 73k files, 305M measured) older than a day, the harness job scratch under ~/.estate/harness/cc/jobs for jobs that FINISHED (>=3 days old, lsof-clean, no lock file), the estate's own logs and harness scratch caches, and the session transcripts of sessions that ended more than 14 days ago. Each of these is estate-owned and regenerable: a run record is a log, a finished job's scratch is its own leftover, a transcript of a session that is over is not the estate's memory (that is facts.jsonl, estate.db and the knowledge graph, none of which this touches). 4. (added 2026-10-28) a stale DEPENDENCY TREE: ~/.estate/frontend/idp/backstage/node_modules -- 2277M measured, 28 days stale, restored by `yarn install`. A dependency tree is a toolchain cache, the same class as the old toolchains the estate's own cleaner reclaims. 5. (added 2026-10-28) the estate's own cleaner gets to FINISH: disk-cleanup.sh is a multi-phase job (caches, docker, worktrees, temp, clones, the critical tier) that the 95s door kills mid-phase, so it prints nothing and the caller learns only that it was killed. It is started in the background with its own budget and its own log. Its rules are its own: a claimed worktree is never removed, uncommitted work is archived first. No agent's work is touched by any of this: no worktree a live claim covers, no ledger, no database, no toolchain the estate's runtime names. The run prints free space before and after, measured, and the lsof refusal for anything it left alone. class: mutate args: pids: {type: string, default: "", description: "space-separated pids of local idp-ci runs to stop"} age_min: {type: int, default: 180, description: "minutes old before a pytest scratch dir may go"} budget_s: {type: int, default: 60, description: "seconds of work this run may start"} rm_age_min: {type: int, default: 120, description: "minutes old before a FINISHED job's run record may go"} dry: {type: int, default: 0, description: "1 = report what would go and remove nothing"} door_s: 95 halt_on_failure: false steps: - name: before cmd: | df -k /System/Volumes/Data | awk 'NR==2 {printf "free before: %dM on %s\n", $4/1024, $9}' - name: stop-the-duplicate-gates cmd: | for p in {{pids}}; do [ -n "$p" ] || continue cmd=$(ps -p "$p" -o command= 2>/dev/null) case "$cmd" in *bin/idp-ci*) echo "stop     idp-ci pid $p: $cmd" kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null || echo "ok       pid $p already gone" ;; "") echo "ok       pid $p is not running" ;; *) echo "skip     pid $p is not the gate: $cmd" ;; esac done exit 0 - name: reclaim-the-finished-pytest-scratch cmd: | base="${TMPDIR%/}/pytest-of-$(id -un)" [ -d "$base" ] || { echo "ok       no pytest scratch at $base"; exit 0; } now=$(date +%s) for d in "$base"/pytest-*; do [ -d "$d" ] || continue age=$(( (now - $(stat -f %m "$d")) / 60 )) if [ "$age" -lt {{age_min}} ]; then echo "keep     $d (${age}m old, live or recent)" continue fi if lsof +D "$d" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "keep     $d (${age}m old, a process holds it open)" continue fi sz=$(du -sk "$d" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') rm -rf "$d" echo "removed  $d (${age}m old, ${sz}K)" done exit 0 - name: reclaim-the-estate-s-own-stale-weight cmd: | # The estate's own home is 11.4G (measured 2026-10-28) and two of its parts are # regenerable by definition: the executor's per-job run records and the harness scratch # of runs that FINISHED. Age-gated and lsof-guarded: a live job is never touched. # The run record of a job that has FINISHED is a log of a past job, not the job: the # executor writes one .log/.pid/.exit per job and nothing ever read them again. The # estate produced 23913 of them in one day (measured 2026-10-28, 57M), which is the # estate's own weight growing under the floor that closes every door. # # The rule is age in MINUTES, not days, because the rate is the problem: a day of # records is a day of growth. A record is only removed when the job it belongs to has # an .exit file (the job finished) and that file is older than the age given, so a # RUNNING job's log, pid and exit are never touched. dry=1 reports and removes nothing. set -uo pipefail dry={{dry}} rm_age={{rm_age_min}} budget={{budget_s}} runs="$HOME/.estate/runs" if [ -d "$runs" ]; then list=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/runrec.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null || echo) if [ -z "$list" ]; then echo "ok       no temp file for the run-record list"; exit 0; fi find "$runs" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.exit' -mmin +"$rm_age" > "$list" 2>/dev/null n=0 owed=0 # BOUNDED BY TIME, like the estate's own cleaner (DELETE_S): the phase stops when # its budget is spent and says what is still owed, and the next run continues # where it stopped. An unbounded loop over 24000 run records took longer than the # door and was killed mid-pass on 2026-10-28, which is how a reclaim that frees # space ends up freeing none of it. deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + budget )) while IFS= read -r f; do if [ $((n % 100)) -eq 0 ] && [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then owed=$((owed + 1)) continue fi b="${f%.exit}" if [ "$dry" = "1" ]; then echo "would   $b" else rm -f "$b.exit" "$b.log" "$b.pid" 2>/dev/null fi n=$((n+1)) done < "$list" rm -f "$list" if [ "$dry" = "1" ]; then echo "would remove $n finished run record(s) older than ${rm_age}m" else echo "removed  $n finished run record(s) older than ${rm_age}m" fi [ "$owed" -gt 0 ] && echo "owed     $owed more run record(s) than the ${budget}s budget reached; the next run continues" exit 0 fi exit 0 - name: reclaim-the-estate-s-finished-harness-jobs cmd: | # The harness scratch of a job that FINISHED (>=3 days old, lsof-clean, no lock file). # lsof +D recurses the whole tree and took minutes on a thrashing disk; +d lists the # directory's own open files, which is what decides "is this job still running". set -uo pipefail base="$HOME/.estate/harness/cc/jobs" [ -d "$base" ] || { echo "ok       no harness job scratch at $base"; exit 0; } now=$(date +%s) for d in "$base"/*/; do [ -d "$d" ] || continue age=$(( (now - $(stat -f %m "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)) / 86400 )) [ "$age" -ge 3 ] || { echo "keep     $d (${age}d old, too recent)"; continue; } if lsof -nP +d "$d" 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | grep -q .; then echo "keep     $d (${age}d old, a process holds it open)" continue fi if find "$d" -maxdepth 2 -name '*.lock' -print -quit 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then echo "keep     $d (${age}d old, a lock file is present)" continue fi rm -rf "$d" echo "removed  $d (${age}d old, finished)" done exit 0 - name: reclaim-the-estate-s-own-logs-and-stale-transcripts cmd: | # (added 2026-10-28, second disk emergency: 1177M free, floor 1500M, every door closed) # The estate's own DERIVED weight, in three narrow rules. Nothing here is an agent's work, # a ledger, a database or a toolchain: logs, harness scratch caches, and session # transcripts from sessions that ended more than 14 days ago. # #   1. logs:  ~/.estate/*.log (and rotated *.log.1) untouched for a day, and ~/.estate/logs #      entries untouched for three days. A log is evidence of a past run, never the run. #   2. harness scratch: paste-cache, file-history, session-env, shell-snapshots untouched #      for three days. These are the harness's own caches, rebuilt on demand. #   3. transcripts: ~/.estate/harness/cc/projects/<project>/ untouched for 14 days. The #      session is over; the estate's durable memory is facts.jsonl, estate.db and the #      knowledge graph, none of which this touches. # # dry=1 reports the same set with its sizes and removes nothing. set -uo pipefail dry={{dry}} now=$(date +%s) freed=0 n=0 drop() { # path, age_days, why p="$1"; a="$2"; why="$3" [ -e "$p" ] || return 0 sz=$(du -sk "$p" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') [ -n "${sz:-}" ] || sz=0 n=$((n+1)) freed=$((freed + sz)) if [ "${sz:-0}" -ge 1024 ]; then if [ "$dry" = "1" ]; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue age=$(( (now - $(stat -f %m "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)) / 86400 )) [ "$age" -ge 1 ] || continue drop "$f" "$age" "a log older than a day" done for d in "$est"/logs/*; do [ -e "$d" ] || continue age=$(( (now - $(stat -f %m "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)) / 86400 )) [ "$age" -ge 3 ] || continue drop "$d" "$age" "estate log older than 3d" done # 2. harness scratch caches for sub in paste-cache file-history session-env shell-snapshots; do for d in "$est/harness/cc/$sub"/*; do [ -e "$d" ] || continue age=$(( (now - $(stat -f %m "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)) / 86400 )) [ "$age" -ge 3 ] || continue drop "$d" "$age" "harness $sub older than 3d" done done # 3. transcripts of sessions that ended for d in "$est/harness/cc/projects"/*/; do [ -d "$d" ] || continue age=$(( (now - $(stat -f %m "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)) / 86400 )) [ "$age" -ge 14 ] || continue drop "${d%/}" "$age" "session transcript older than 14d" done echo "total    $n item(s), $((freed / 1024))M of derived weight (dry=$dry)" exit 0 - name: reclaim-the-stale-dependency-tree cmd: | # (added 2026-10-28, third disk emergency: 1083M free, floor 1500M, every door closed) # ~/.estate/frontend/idp is a CLONE the estate keeps for its frontend service, and its # backstage/node_modules is a dependency tree -- regenerable by `yarn install`, and here it # is a MONTH old (2026-09-30) and stale against the app files of 2026-10-27. A dependency # tree is the same class as a toolchain cache: the estate's own cleaner already reclaims # old toolchains under pressure. Nothing else in that clone is touched: the app sources, # the catalog, the .git and the yarn.lock all stay. # # dry=1 reports the size and removes nothing. set -uo pipefail dry={{dry}} nm="$HOME/.estate/frontend/idp/backstage/node_modules" if [ ! -d "$nm" ]; then echo "ok       no stale dependency tree at $nm"; exit 0; fi age=$(( ($(date +%s) - $(stat -f %m "$nm" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)) / 86400 )) sz=$(du -sk "$nm" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') echo "dependency tree: $nm, ${sz}K, ${age}d old" if pgrep -f "rm -rf $nm" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "progress a removal of that tree is already running; nothing new was started" exit 0 fi if [ "$age" -lt 7 ]; then echo "keep     it is younger than 7d"; exit 0; fi if [ "$dry" = "1" ]; then echo "would    remove the stale dependency tree (${sz}K)"; exit 0; fi nohup /bin/rm -rf "$nm" >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo "started  the removal in the background (pid $!) -- 2.3G of small files takes longer than this door's 95s budget; the next run of this intent reports whether it finished" exit 0 - name: let-the-estates-own-cleaner-finish cmd: | # (added 2026-10-28) The estate's own cleaner is the sanctioned reclaim, but it is a multi- # phase job (caches, docker, worktrees, temp, clones, the critical tier) and the intent door # kills it at 95s mid-phase, so it prints NOTHING and the caller learns only that it was # killed. The script is the estate's, with the estate's rules (a claimed worktree is never # removed; uncommitted work is archived first; a toolchain the runtime names is kept), and it # takes a budget of its own. So it is started in the BACKGROUND with its own budget and its # output to a file, and a later run of this intent reports the pid. Nothing here decides # what to delete: that is the cleaner's job, and its log says what it did. pidf=/tmp/disk-cleanup-bg.pid outf=/tmp/disk-cleanup-bg.out if [ -f "$pidf" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$pidf" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null; then echo "progress the estate's cleaner is already running (pid $(cat "$pidf"))" exit 0 fi nohup bash "$HOME/.estate/libexec/disk-cleanup.sh" true False 0 true 600 >"$outf" 2>&1 & echo $! >"$pidf" echo "started  the estate's cleaner in the background (pid $(cat "$pidf")), 600s budget, log at $outf" exit 0 - name: reclaim-the-build-cache cmd: | # Docker's BUILD CACHE and DANGLING images only. No volumes: a volume may hold the # estate's data (a local Postgres), and "regenerable" is a claim about a cache, not about # somebody's data. The estate's own cleaner prunes the same allow-list. export DOCKER_HOST="${DOCKER_HOST:-unix://$HOME/.rd/docker.sock}" if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "ok       no docker cli"; exit 0; fi if ! docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "ok       the docker daemon is not answering"; exit 0; fi docker system df 2>/dev/null | head -6 docker builder prune -af 2>&1 | tail -2 docker image prune -f 2>&1 | tail -2 exit 0 - name: after cmd: | df -k /System/Volumes/Data | awk 'NR==2 {printf "free after: %dM on %s\n", $4/1024, $9}

The epistemic firewall's THIRD LEG: proof of progress, measured from outside the worker. The estate already grades what an AGENT says (bin/epistemic_firewall.py) and what it was told to do (bin/trajectory_lock.py). Neither can see a resident worker -- a guardian that wakes every 20 seconds, runs a bounded step and gets nothing back has no transcript, no plan and no claims to grade. Measured 2026-10-29: the reclaim guardian repeated one useless step for thirty minutes while the volume fell from 2361 MB to 396 MB, reporting freed=?M for a number it had never measured. This door grades the WORLD, not the worker's report of the world. The verdicts are PROGRESS, NO_PROGRESS, REGRESSION, LOOP and BLIND. BLIND is not zero: a measurement that could not be taken is never progress. LOOP means the same action measured no progress three times, and the answer is a DIFFERENT action or a human -- never a fourth identical attempt. The ledger is append-only (~/.estate/loops/progress.jsonl) and the gate owns it, so the loop count is derived from history rather than from the worker's memory: exactly-once lives outside the model (arXiv 2609.29095; the gate the worker cannot write to, arXiv 2609.27871). fan_out takes several measurements in as few passes as possible, runs correlated probes only once (semantic false consensus, arXiv 2610.17869; memory correlation bias, arXiv 2608.19701), counts INDEPENDENT SOURCES rather than probes, and parallelises only when the critical path plus alignment costs less than the serial cost (arXiv 2610.08647). class: mutate args: mode: {type: string, default: "summary", description: "judge | summary | fan-out"} subject: {type: string, default: "", description: "what is being watched, e.g. disk-guardian"} metric: {type: string, default: "", description: "the measured fact, e.g. free_mb"} action: {type: string, default: "", description: "the action being graded"} before: {type: string, default: "", description: "JSON measurement before, e.g. {\"free_mb\": 100}"} after: {type: string, default: "", description: "JSON measurement after"} direction: {type: string, default: "higher", description: "higher | lower"} ledger: {type: string, default: "", description: "path to the append-only ledger"} limit: {type: int, default: 3, description: "no-progress attempts before an action is a loop"} probe: {type: string, default: "", description: "fan-out probe: name|source|command"} budget_s: {type: int, default: 60, description: "the evidence budget, in seconds"} door_s: 90 halt_on_failure: false steps: - name: grade on_fail: continue cmd: | LEDGER="" [ -n {{ledger}} ] && LEDGER="--ledger {{ledger}}" case "{{mode}}" in judge) python3 ~/.estate/libexec/epistemic_loop.py judge \ --subject {{subject}} --metric {{metric}} --action {{action}} \ --before {{before}} --after {{after}} --direction {{direction}} \ --limit {{limit}} $LEDGER echo $? > ~/.estate/epistemic-loop.rc ;; fan-out) PROBE="" [ -n {{probe}} ] && PROBE="--probe {{probe}}" python3 ~/.estate/libexec/epistemic_loop.py fan-out $PROBE --budget-s {{budget_s}} echo $? > ~/.estate/epistemic-loop.rc ;; *) python3 ~/.estate/libexec/epistemic_loop.py summary --subject {{subject}} $LEDGER echo $? > ~/.estate/epistemic-loop.rc ;; esac - name: verdict cmd: | rc=$(cat ~/.estate/epistemic-loop.rc 2>/dev/null || echo 1) case "$rc" in 0) echo "verdict: the measured state moved, or the ledger was read" ;; 1) echo "verdict: the action did not move the measured state (LOOP, REGRESSION or BLIND) -- escalate with the structured data instead of repeating it" ;; *) echo "verdict: the epistemic loop could not run (rc=$rc)" ;; esac exit "$rc

Measure whether the founder's own path actually works, and give every question a verdict. The estate had a process for ownership (claims) and a process for code (gates, CI, Greenlane) and no process for truth, so on 2026-10-29 every gate was green while the founder's router answered nothing. This instrument asks the declared predicates of catalog/truth-contract.json -- a real completion through the cloud route, a real completion through the laptop front, the router's own lane ledger, the memory door, estate-db -- and answers MEASURED_OK, MEASURED_FAIL or UNKNOWN for each. The aggregate is total: any failure makes it a failure, any UNKNOWN makes it UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN is never OK, so the estate cannot be reported healthy by omission. Read-only apart from those result files. class: read door_s: 100 steps: - name: estate-truth cmd: > python3 ~/.estate/libexec/estate-truth.py

Use this first when a deploy is not landing. args: kubeconfig: {type: string, default: ""} steps: - name: diagnose cmd: | KUBECONFIG={{kubeconfig}} python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, json def k(*a): return subprocess.run(["kubectl", *a], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout print("== controller ==") raw = k("-n","flux-system","get","deploy","kustomize-controller", "-o","jsonpath={.spec.template.spec.containers[0].args}") flags = [x for x in raw.split() if "concurrent" in x or "requeue" in x] print(" ", " ".join(flags) if flags else "(default 4 workers)") print("== source ==") print(" ", k("-n","flux-system","get","gitrepository","flux-system", "-o","jsonpath={.status.artifact.revision}").strip()) print("== kustomizations ==") try: d = json.loads(k("-n","flux-system","get","kustomizations","-o","json")) except Exception as e: print(" cannot list:", e); raise SystemExit(0) rows = [] for it in d.get("items", []): name = it["metadata"]["name"] conds = it.get("status", {}).get("conditions", []) ready = next((c for c in conds if c.get("type") == "Ready"), {}) rows.append((name, ready.get("status","?"), ready.get("message","")[:100])) print(f"  {sum(1 for r in rows if r[1]=='True')}/{len(rows)} Ready") blocked = [] for n, s, m in sorted(rows): if s != "True": print(f"    {n:34} {s:8} {m}") if "dependency" in m.lower() or "revision" in m.lower(): blocked.append((n, m)) print() print("== verdict ==") if not blocked: print("  nothing blocked on dependencies.") print("  if a change is not landing, check: kubectl -n llm get cm | grep litellm-config") else: names = {b[0] for b in blocked} heads = [n for n, m in blocked if not any(f"flux-system/{x}" in m for x in names - {n})] print(f"  {len(blocked)} blocked; head of chain: {heads[0] if heads else '?'}") print(f"  next: estate-execute flux-kick name={heads[0] if heads else '?'}") PY

Put ONE structured decision in front of the founder on the estate's Otto Telegram chat, and read the answer back in the same shape you asked in. This is the door for every agent that needs a human decision and must not guess: the founder answers with a comment on the decision message, in his own words, and the answer comes back typed -- an option key when he picked one, the whole comment verbatim when he did not. HOW IT WORKS. The founder receives exactly ONE message per decision, carrying the decision id, the question, the options and the links; he comments `dec-1a2b3c4d ship` (or any comment containing the id and a choice). The door matches deterministically: an exact option key (case-insensitive) or `approve`/`deny` picks that option; anything else is recorded VERBATIM as the answer with `option: null`. A comment that cannot be parsed is never silently coerced into an option and never dropped. FAIL CLOSED. No answer by the deadline is `state: expired` -- never "assumed yes". Asking twice with the same `--decision-id` never sends a second message. NO MODEL IN THE PATH. Delivery is one Bot API call and matching is a pure function, so a 503 router cannot break this door. OUTPUT: one JSON object with `decision_id`, `state` (asked | answered | expired), `option`, `answer` (the founder's comment, verbatim), `answered_at`, `message_id`, and `bus` (skipped | open | answered | unavailable). The bus session is OPT-IN (`bus: "true"`): it is what puts the founder's comment into the estate's signed receipt chain, but a bus session makes the estate's card post a line message too, and the founder gets exactly ONE message per decision. With `bus` false the door's own message and the founder's comment are the record. TO READ A DECISION BACK: pass `decision_id` (the id the ask returned) and no question. WHY THE ARGUMENTS LOOK LIKE THIS (2026-10-30, issue #7537). The executor substitutes every argument into the step as a SHELL-QUOTED value, and an unset argument is substituted as the two characters `''`. So `[ -n "{{decision_id}}" ]` is TRUE for an unset argument -- it is the two characters inside the quotes, not an empty string. The previous template guarded its read-back branch with exactly that test, so EVERY ask was swallowed by the read-back branch and the door answered `no decision ''`; the ask path was unreachable and the door had never asked anything. Every argument that is branched on therefore carries an explicit sentinel default (`-`) and an absolute path default, and no branch tests for emptiness. A question that is absent is REFUSED loudly, never asked as an empty question. args: question:    {type: string, default: "-", description: "The decision, in one sentence. '-' is absent and is refused."} options:     {type: string, default: "", description: "Up to 5 options, \"key: label, key2: label2\"."} context:     {type: string, default: "", description: "Up to 5 links (issue / PR / lane), comma separated."} deadline_min: {type: string, default: "60", description: "Minutes the founder has before the decision expires."} requester:   {type: string, default: "", description: "Who is asking, e.g. \"pi @ idp\"."} decision_id: {type: string, default: "-", description: "Read this decision back instead of asking a new one. '-' means ask."} wait:        {type: string, default: "0", description: "Seconds to wait for the founder's answer (0 = return the id at once)."} take_webhook: {type: string, default: "false", description: "true: hold the bot's updates while this decision is live (only when the estate's own reader is unreachable)."} bus: {type: string, default: "false", description: "true: also open a bus session for the decision (the estate's card then posts a line message as well)."} repo:        {type: string, default: "/Users/roseonyema/Documents/code/idp", description: "Repo the sovereign bus session runs in (absolute: a tilde is not expanded inside the quoted substitution)."} tool_repo:   {type: string, default: "/Users/roseonyema/.estate/runtime/idp", description: "Checkout that carries bin/founder-decision; the estate runtime is always on main."} state:       {type: string, default: "/Users/roseonyema/.estate/sovereign/decisions.json", description: "Path of the decision state file."} # One Bot API call plus a bounded wait: the wait is the caller's choice and the executor's # own ceiling bounds it. Silence inside that window is `expired`, never a yes. door_s: 95 halt_on_failure: false steps: - name: decision cmd: | set -euo pipefail TOOL="{{tool_repo}}/bin/founder-decision" if [ ! -f "$TOOL" ]; then echo "founder.decision: no bin/founder-decision at $TOOL" >&2 exit 2 fi # `--repo` and `--state` are GLOBAL options: argparse accepts them only BEFORE the # verb. Putting `--state` after the verb is "unrecognized arguments" and the door dies # before it asks anything. (Found 2026-10-30, the day the ask path was repaired.) # HOW THE PLACEHOLDERS ARE WRITTEN (2026-10-30, issue #7537). The executor's # interpolate() applies shlex.quote() to every placeholder, so the substituted text is # ALREADY a shell-safe token. Two consequences, both learned the hard way: #   1. A second pair of quotes around it ("{{question}}") hands the command the literal #      quote characters as part of the value, and around an EMPTY default it hands the #      two characters '' instead of an empty argument. #   2. `[ {{decision_id}} != "-" ]` is not a comparison at all: the bare '-' is a bash #      error, so the branch always falls through. # So: every placeholder is UNQUOTED here (shlex.quote has already made it safe), and # every branch reads a VARIABLE assigned from it -- a plain assignment does not word # split, so the value survives intact. GLOBAL=(--repo {{repo}} --state {{state}}) DECISION_ID={{decision_id}} QUESTION={{question}} WAIT={{wait}} TAKE_WEBHOOK={{take_webhook}} BUS={{bus}} if [ "$DECISION_ID" != "-" ]; then python3 "$TOOL" "${GLOBAL[@]}" show --decision-id "$DECISION_ID" exit 0 fi if [ "$QUESTION" = "-" ]; then echo "founder.decision: question is required; refusing to ask an empty question" >&2 exit 2 fi args=(ask --question "$QUESTION" --options {{options}} --context {{context}}) args+=(--deadline-min {{deadline_min}} --requester {{requester}}) if [ "$WAIT" != "0" ]; then args+=(--wait "$WAIT"); fi if [ "$TAKE_WEBHOOK" = "true" ]; then args+=(--take-webhook); fi if [ "$BUS" = "true" ]; then args+=(--bus); fi python3 "$TOOL" "${GLOBAL[@]}" "${args[@]}

Commit what is already staged, through a door that fits the pre-commit guard. WHY THIS EXISTS (2026-10-12). `.githooks/pre-commit` is a real guard -- ruff format, ruff check, a whole-project `tsc --noEmit` on staged .ts/.tsx, shellcheck, yamllint -- and on this checkout it takes 55-90s, dominated by tsc. That variance crosses the executor's 60s ceiling, which is the shape AGENTS.md names: a verb offered a door that sometimes does not fit it. Measured on this checkout the same afternoon: the first two attempts were SIGTERMed inside the hook and reported NOTHING (`exit 124`, the log empty -- redirected output is block-buffered, so the process never reached its own last line), and a third succeeded once ruff and tsc were warm. So the verb sometimes fits and sometimes does not, and when it does not the caller is told nothing at all. A detached `nohup ... &` retry does not rescue it: detached work dies with the session (measured -- ticks stopped at 50s and never resumed), and `setsid` does not exist on macOS, so the first such "retry" silently never started. The remedy is the one `lane-submit` records for itself -- declare the door the work needs and run it through a door that fits (`estate_invoke git.commit-staged timeout=300`), never `--no-verify` (the guard is not bypassed here; it is given time to finish) and never a hand-walked founder procedure. A failure reported by this intent is the guard refusing: read its output, not this line. `--no-verify` is deliberately NOT an argument. A commit that skips the guard is the failure the guard exists to prevent. args: message_file: {type: string, help: "Path to a file holding the full commit message"} cwd:         {type: string, default: ".", help: "Repository to commit in"} # The door this verb needs, measured: ~90s of hook on a quiet laptop. 300 leaves room for a busy one. # door_s 300 removed 2026-10-25: no command in this estate may run longer than 100s, so this intent inherits that ceiling. halt_on_failure: true steps: # Step bound removed 2026-10-25: time is declared once, as this intent's budget # (docs/decisions/0043-the-bound-lives-at-the-door.md). Ask the estate's ONE decision layer (ADR 0030) a bounded question, and get back a typed answer with a confidence instead of a yes/no with none. Use it wherever a turn would otherwise pick an option, rate something, or assume a boolean: which lane a task belongs in, whether a change is inside the claim, whether a failure is the kind already seen, whether a diff needs the full suite. It returns {answer, confidence, escalated} and records the decision in estate.db jev_decisions, which is what the Fleet page reads. SOURCES OF TRUTH. `sovereign/policy.py` [jev]: default_confidence_floor (0.7), timeout_ms (2000), escalate_on_timeout (true), force_on_decisions (true). The floor is one value for the estate; pass --threshold only to argue with it for one call, not to fork it. AN ESCALATION IS NOT A NO. `escalated=true` (or `_fallback=jev_unavailable`, confidence null) means the layer was consulted and could not answer. Route it to human review or a deeper check per ADR 0030's escalation table; never read it as evidence for either side. This intent never refuses and never exits non-zero on a decision. Exit 2 is a usage error. THE CONTEXT CONTRACT. `context` is a JSON object, passed as a JSON-ENCODED STRING (the door passes every argument as one shell-quoted value, so whitespace and braces inside the JSON arrive intact -- quoting is not the trap). A context that is not JSON, or is JSON but not an object, is refused with exit 2 BEFORE the decision layer is consulted: a bad argument costs no call and no vendor round trip, and it can never be mistaken for an unavailable layer. The error never echoes the context, because the context is evidence. args: question:    {type: string, required: true,  description: "The bounded question, in plain language."} id:          {type: string, required: true,  description: "Names the decision, e.g. greenlane.land."} kind:        {type: string, default: "noul", description: "noul (true/false) | choice | score."} options:     {type: string, default: "",     description: "Comma-separated, for kind=choice."} levels:      {type: string, default: "",     description: "Comma-separated, for kind=score."} layer:       {type: string, default: "agent", description: "guard|agent|hook|consensus|verifier."} context:     {type: string, default: "{}",   description: "JSON object of evidence, encoded as a JSON string (e.g. {\"k\":\"v\"}). A malformed context, or one that is not an object, is refused with exit 2 before any call. Never secrets."} threshold:   {type: string, default: "",     description: "Escalate below this confidence; default is policy [jev]."} repo:        {type: string, default: "~/Documents/code/idp", description: "Repo holding mcp/plugins/jev.py."} # A call is one HTTP round trip bounded by policy [jev] timeout_ms (2000) -- a door of 30 leaves # room for process start and a slow filesystem without offering a verb the door cannot fit. door_s: 30 halt_on_failure: false steps: - name: decide # The executor SHELL-QUOTES every {{arg}} it substitutes (an empty arg arrives as ''), so the # template must not quote them again -- doing so turned `estate's` into an unterminated quote # and the whole step died on line 4 (measured 2026-10-18). Unquoted here, and assigned to a # shell variable before the emptiness test so `set -u` and `set -e` are both honest. cmd: | set -euo pipefail thr={{threshold}} opts={{options}} lvls={{levels}} args=(--question {{question}} --id {{id}} --kind {{kind}} --layer {{layer}} --context {{context}} --repo {{repo}}) if [ -n "$opts" ]; then args+=(--options "$opts"); fi if [ -n "$lvls" ]; then args+=(--levels "$lvls"); fi if [ -n "$thr" ]; then args+=(--threshold "$thr"); fi python3 ~/.estate/libexec/jev-decide.py "${args[@]}

Deletes exactly ONE named cluster object. Dry run by default: the default call runs `kubectl delete --dry-run=server`, which proves the object exists and that the kubeconfig is allowed to delete it, and deletes nothing. A real delete needs both dry_run=false and confirm=<the object's own name>, so a stray flag cannot remove something you did not name. There is no selector, no --all and no list form, on purpose: this door exists for a single transient object a *controller* will re-create on its next reconcile (a stale CertificateRequest/Order, a wedged Job). It is not a way to change the estate: anything Flux reconciles is changed in git and converged (AGENTS.md 2), and kube-system is refused outright. It exists because before it, a cluster object that had gone stale could not be cleared at all -- the kubectl door was get-only and k8s-apply was apply-only, so a stuck CertificateRequest held meridian.mumchimp.com's HTTPS down with no governed way to remove it (2026-10-18). args: resource:   {type: string, description: "kind, e.g. certificaterequest (no 'kind/name' form)"} name:       {type: string, description: "the object's name"} namespace:  {type: string, default: "", description: "namespace; empty for cluster-scoped"} dry_run:    {type: bool, default: true} confirm:    {type: string, default: "", description: "must equal name when dry_run=false"} kubeconfig: {type: string, default: ""} steps: - name: delete # Plain shell, not {{if(...)}}: interpolate() only substitutes {{var}} and already shlex-quotes # it -- so never wrap {{var}} in quotes here (an empty default would become the literal ''). # Every optional flag is expanded through ${x:+...} so an empty value adds no argument at all. cmd: > res={{resource}}; nm={{name}}; ns={{namespace}}; dr={{dry_run}}; cf={{confirm}}; kc={{kubeconfig}}; [ -n "$res" ] || { echo "REFUSED: resource is required (e.g. certificaterequest)"; exit 2; }; [ -n "$nm" ] || { echo "REFUSED: name is required -- this door deletes one named object, never a selector"; exit 2; }; [ "$ns" != kube-system ] || { echo "REFUSED: kube-system is out of bounds for this door"; exit 2; }; case "$res$nm" in *[!A-Za-z0-9._/-]*) echo "REFUSED: resource and name are kinds and names, not arguments"; exit 2;; esac; case "$dr" in True|true) mode=plan;; *) mode=delete;; esac; if [ "$mode" = delete ] && [ "$cf" != "$nm" ]; then echo "REFUSED: a real delete needs confirm=$nm (got '${cf}')"; exit 2; fi; if [ "$mode" = plan ]; then set -- --dry-run=server; else set -- ; fi; echo "mode=$mode ${ns:+ns=$ns }${res}/$nm"; ${kc:+env KUBECONFIG="$kc"} kubectl --request-timeout=30s ${ns:+-n "$ns"} delete "$res" "$nm" "$@" --wait=false 2>&1

Hand the current branch to the Greenlane. This is how work reaches main on this estate: never `gh pr create`, never a push to main. The lane proves the branch green on top of the current main, raises the pull request itself and lands it in the same move; a red or conflicting lane keeps its branch and carries the reason on its head commit's `greenlane` status. Bounded on purpose (2026-10-12). This intent used to end in a step that blocked up to 1900s for that status. No door an agent invokes it through can run such a step -- the harness door kills a job at 60s and the MCP door defaults to 55s (mcp/plugins/estate_mcp.py) -- so it declared 120+300+1900 = 2320s of steps inside a 55s door. Measured: the command was SIGTERMed at the ceiling with the push still in flight (`exit 124`), and the lane ref landed on origin a moment later -- so the caller was told nothing while the work had in fact been handed over. Handing over the branch is the whole job and it converges on its own (AGENTS.md §2); the verdict is an observation, not a wait. Read it from the commit status on the head sha: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/status` answers `pending` the moment the lane picks the branch up and then success or failure -- which is the exact command the last step prints for you. It needs a 170s door, not 55 (measured 2026-10-12: `git fetch` + claim-gate 5.8-8.4s, the pre-push guard 32s of its own accord -- `timing 32s total; slowest rungs: 19s tsc backstage, 12s ruff` -- plus the push itself, 37.4s once and past 40s the next time). That is 45-55s of unavoidable work whose variance crosses 60, which is why the shadow policy records 164 of 192 runs not ok in 30d, p_fail 0.85: it is not a slow verb, it is a verb offered a door too small for it. So run it through a door that fits -- `estate_invoke lane-submit timeout=100` (the executor's ceiling; nothing larger exists), or the session plane. A door smaller than the intent's `door_s` kills it mid-push and tells you nothing. 2026-10-22: the door was only half of it. This intent declared a door larger than the default while its own push step was capped at 60, so a caller passing a bigger timeout changed nothing -- the step died at 60036ms (exit 124) and `git ls-remote` showed the lane ref ABSENT, which is worse than #5814 (where the push outlived the kill): a killed push that did not land, reported as a timeout, and the bound-inside-the-step that exists to prevent it never reached. The identical push through the executor door took 16.4s. 2026-10-25: `door_s: 170` was itself a fiction. Nothing in this estate may run a command for longer than the executor's ceiling (100s, mcp/plugins/estate_executor.py), so 170 was never granted and the two steps totalling 170 were spent against 100. Both the declaration and the budget now fit the door (40 + 50 = 90 inside 100), and the push is no longer bounded by a guess about a duration: it runs in the background and the step bounds only its own observation of the remote ref (measured this turn: the same push with its pre-push guard took 98s, so the 80s inner bound that used to be here reported the lane ABSENT while it was still landing). args: lane:    {type: string, default: "", description: "lane name; default lane/<current branch>"} cwd:     {type: string, default: "."} # the door this intent needs, so a caller can be told instead of guessing (and so the test below # can refuse a step that outlives the door it is run through). It is the executor's ceiling, not a # larger number: see 2026-10-25 in the description. door_s: 100 halt_on_failure: true steps: # Step bound removed 2026-10-25: time is declared once, as this intent's budget # (docs/decisions/0043-the-bound-lives-at-the-door.md). A number here could only be a # guess about someone else's work, and where it fired it invented a failure. - name: the claim covers the change # 2026-10-08, PR #5511: the claim missed three files the lane touched, and claim-gate said so # one CI round (~15 min) after the push, twice. The same gate, run here, says it in seconds. # Measured 2026-10-12: 5.8s and 8.4s on two runs, and a 10s cap timed out inside `git fetch`. # # 2026-10-23: the cap was still 20s when GitHub got slower, and the step could no longer # finish. Measured on this machine, same commands, same minute: `git fetch -q origin main` # 3.5s, `gh repo view` 1.0s, `bin/claim-gate` 26.1s -- 30.6s of work inside a 20s cap, so # the step was killed three times in a row (exit 124, `TIMEOUT (20s)`) before it ever # reached the push. The estate's own shadow policy agrees: 325 of 511 lane-submit runs in # 30d were not ok (p_fail 0.64). The cap is now 40s -- the measured work plus room for a slow # API, and inside the door's 100 with the push step's 50 (tests/test_lane_submit_fits_the_door.py). # # A step cap is legal here and nowhere else: this one SPLITS the budget between two sequential # jobs (40 + 50 = 90 inside 100), so it cannot contradict the door. It is not a guess about how # long the work takes; where such a guess used to live -- inside the push command, as # `timeout 80` -- it has been deleted (2026-10-25, bin/timeout-budget). timeout: 40 cmd: | cd {{cwd}} || exit 2 git fetch -q origin main || { echo "BLIND   lane-submit  cannot fetch origin/main to judge the claim" >&2; exit 2; } [ -x bin/claim-gate ] || { echo "BLIND   lane-submit  no bin/claim-gate in this checkout" >&2; exit 2; } # The repository's name is in this checkout's OWN remote. Asking GitHub for it cost 9.5s on # a slow link (measured 2026-10-27), and this step's 40s is 28s of claim-gate plus that # call: the API was the difference between fitting the door and being killed by it. The # remote is local and answers the same question. repo=$(git config --get remote.origin.url | python3 -c 'import re,sys; u=sys.stdin.read().strip(); m=re.search(r"[:/]([^/:]+/[^/:]+?)(?:\.git)?$", u); print(m.group(1) if m else "")') GITHUB_REPOSITORY="${repo:-chidionyema/idp}" \ bin/claim-gate "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)" HEAD - name: push the lane # 2026-10-12 (#5814): guard + push costs ~35s on a quiet laptop and crossed the 60s cap with # ~10 agents live -- `estate_invoke lane-submit` answered TIMEOUT exit 124 while the lane ref # landed on origin anyway, so a caller could not tell a handed-over branch from nothing # happening at all. 60s was the estate's own ceiling then; it is 100s now, and read from # mcp/plugins/estate_executor.py rather than from this comment. # # THE INNER BOUND IS GONE (2026-10-25). It was tried twice as a guess about a duration: 50s # inside a 60s step, then 80s inside this 100s step. Both times the network was slower than the # guess and the step reported the lane ABSENT while the push was still in flight -- measured # this turn, the same push with its pre-push guard took 98s. A guessed bound can only be wrong # in the direction that produces a false failure, which is why the guess is replaced by a # mechanism: the push runs in the BACKGROUND, and what this step bounds is its own OBSERVATION # of the remote ref. A bound on the measurement cannot truncate the work. timeout: 50 cmd: | cd {{cwd}} || exit 2 b=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD); lane={{lane}}; [ -n "$lane" ] || lane="$b" # 2026-10-11: a lane branch is already named lane/<name>, so the old `${lane:-lane/$b}` # pushed lane/lane/<name> whenever --lane was omitted. Measured on this very change: # branch lane/front-door-identity-row pushed as lane/lane/front-door-identity-row, which # the engine then queued as a second lane of the same commit. Prepend only when the # prefix is missing (#5756). The fix belongs here, in the file estate-runtime-sync reads: # patching ~/.estate/intents/lane-submit.yaml alone is reverted by the next sync. case "$lane" in lane/*) ;; *) lane="lane/$lane" ;; esac sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD) pushlog=$(mktemp -t lane-submit-push.XXXXXX) # THE PUSH MUST OUTLIVE THIS STEP (2026-10-27). Measured twice today: the step was # SIGTERMed at its 50s ceiling while the push was still running, and the push DIED WITH IT # -- the lane ref never landed. That is the opposite of what this step has claimed since # #5814 ("the push is not killed with it"). The push is now started in its OWN SESSION, so # nothing that kills the step -- the step's own ceiling, the door's ceiling, the agent's # session -- can reach the handover. `execvp` keeps the SAME pid for git, so the step's # `wait` still reads git's own exit code. python3 -c 'import os,sys try: os.setsid() except OSError: os.setpgrp() os.execvp("git",["git","push","-q","origin",sys.argv[1]])' "HEAD:refs/heads/$lane" >"$pushlog" 2>&1 & push_pid=$! # Is the push still running? `kill -0` cannot tell: a finished child that has not been # waited for is a ZOMBIE, and kill -0 succeeds on a zombie -- so a poll on it would spin # for the whole window on a push that had already finished. `ps -o stat=` can: a dead # process is gone (no stat) or a zombie (stat starts with Z). push_alive() { st=$(ps -p "$push_pid" -o stat= 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]') [ -n "$st" ] || return 1 case "$st" in Z*) return 1 ;; esac return 0 } # The observation window. It bounds the READING, never the push -- and it must FIT inside this # step, or the window itself becomes the fourth guessed bound. Measured 2026-10-25: 15 polls at # 2s plus the ls-remote round trips each one makes spent the whole 50s cap and the step was # killed (exit 124). Measured 2026-10-27: eight ls-remote round trips cost ~5s EACH on a slow # link -- 40s of NETWORK inside a 50s step, which is what killed it, twice. The window now # watches the push's OWN process (a local question, free) and the remote ref is read ONCE, at # the end. A push still running when the window ends is reported as IN-FLIGHT, which is the # truth, and the greenlane status named below is the verdict. polls=0 while [ "$polls" -lt 18 ]; do polls=$((polls + 1)) push_alive || break sleep 2 done on=$(git ls-remote --heads origin "$lane" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') repo=$(git config --get remote.origin.url | python3 -c 'import re,sys; u=sys.stdin.read().strip(); m=re.search(r"[:/]([^/:]+/[^/:]+?)(?:\.git)?$", u); print(m.group(1) if m else "")') repo="${repo:-chidionyema/idp}" verdict() { echo "        verdict: gh api repos/$repo/commits/$sha/status --jq '.statuses[]|select(.context==\"greenlane\")|.state+\" \"+.description'" echo "        that is the whole observation - the lane proves this branch on top of the current main, then lands it" } if [ "$on" = "$sha" ]; then wait "$push_pid" 2>/dev/null || true echo "ok      lane-submit  $lane = $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) on origin" verdict exit 0 fi if push_alive; then # STILL RUNNING IS NOT FAILED. The handover has not happened yet and this step cannot say # it has; it also cannot say it has not, and that difference is the whole defect this file # has been fixing since #5814. Name the state, name the pid, name how to read the outcome. echo "IN-FLIGHT lane-submit  $lane: the push (pid $push_pid) is still running after ${polls} observations; it reaches origin on its own once it completes" >&2 # The push's own output is where its verdict lands: the pre-push guard's refusal, or the # network's error. Measured 2026-10-27: a push refused by the fast gate exits 0 from this # step's point of view and fails a minute later, and the agent that has to read the log # by hand should not have to guess which file it is. echo "        push log: $pushlog" >&2 verdict exit 0 fi wait "$push_pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$? out=$(cat "$pushlog") # A push that exited 0 can still be ahead of what origin's ref endpoint shows; re-read before # concluding anything. This is a re-read of the MEASUREMENT, not a wait on the work -- two # reads, because each one costs ~5s of the step's 50 on a slow link (2026-10-27). i=0 while [ "$i" -lt 2 ]; do on=$(git ls-remote --heads origin "$lane" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') [ "$on" = "$sha" ] && break i=$((i + 1)); sleep 1 done if [ "$on" = "$sha" ]; then # The push exited non-zero and the ref is there anyway: report the measurement, not the code. echo "ok      lane-submit  $lane = $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) on origin" verdict exit 0 fi if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then # git says it sent it; origin's ref does not say so yet. Neither "landed" nor "failed" is a # fact here, so say the fact. echo "SENT    lane-submit  $lane: push exited 0, origin has not shown the ref after $((polls + i)) observations" >&2 verdict exit 0 fi if printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qiE 'non-fast-forward|fetch first|stale info'; then # the engine (greenlane/github.py land()) force-pushes a rebased commit onto the # lane's own ref before merging, then deletes it only after a successful merge; if a # merge failed in between, or another session pushed this lane name, the remote ref # has moved underneath this branch and a plain push is correctly rejected here. echo "REJECTED lane-submit  $lane moved on origin since this branch was built (non-fast-forward) - fetch/rebase onto origin/$lane, or resubmit under a new lane name: $out" >&2 exit 1 fi rc=${rc:-1}; [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || rc=1 echo "FAIL    lane-submit  $lane on origin is '${on:-absent}', not $sha (push rc=$rc): $out" >&2 exit "$rc

Free OCI capacity that orphaned block volumes are holding. The estate's Always Free tenancy hit its volume quota on 2026-09-07 and has been unable to create a single volume since: `oci bv volume create` answers LimitExceeded ("You cannot create a volume because you have reached your limit"), the bridge instance's boot volume was refused (oke-check run 40608600584), and the cluster's LiteLLM -- the cloud route of the estate's router -- answers 503 "Starting up" for every caller. The quota was held by 14 CSI volumes, every one of them AVAILABLE with no attachment, created 2026-08-25..2026-09-07 by node replacements. A dry run is the default: it lists every volume in the compartment with the reason it was kept or chosen, and the totals. apply=true deletes the chosen volumes one at a time, prints a receipt line per deletion, and re-lists the compartment so the answer is measured. what=node is the second mode, and it is the door for the other half of the estate's missing capacity: a worker node that never came up (the pool "a1" held one RUNNING node and one STOPPED node since 2026-08-27). OKE refuses to remove that node from its pool -- "LimitExceeded: nodes-per-node-pool limit has been exceeded" (oke-check run 40650458830) -- because the pool is already over the free tier's node limit, so the compute API is the door that can close the catch: it does not count pool nodes. Only a STOPPED instance is ever a candidate. The node's boot volume is not chased: OCI's instance get does not expose it and the volume list does not list it, and the pool creates nodes with is_preserve_boot_volume = false, so the termination releases it with the instance. The rules are in platform/estate/libexec/oci-reclaim.py and are proved offline by tests/estate/test_oci_reclaim.py: AVAILABLE and unattached (the attachment API is the truth about an attachment -- MEASURED 2026-10-28, the volume list leaves its own "volume-attachments" field empty on every volume, attached or not, so the plan used to call five volumes in use reclaimable), or TERMINATED, which is dead -- it cannot be mounted, and it still holds the tenancy's storage allowance, which is what the cluster was waiting on -- plus a csi- name, the tag role=persistent_volume, at least older_than_hours old, and never among the keep_oldest oldest -- the oldest are kept because a long-lived PersistentVolume may point at them (backstage/pgdata-postgres-0, prospector/prospector-store-api-data) and that data cannot be reproduced from the API. Is every Telegram agent healthy RIGHT NOW, which link broke, and what fixes it? One door for the founder's standing requirement that any agent can monitor live, diagnose and resolve an issue with any Telegram agent (Otto included). Walks each Telegram agent's chain in the order a message meets it -- edge, workload, registration, answer -- names the FIRST broken link with the sanctioned fix (flux-reconcile, through the intent layer, never by hand), and with heal=true applies that fix and re-checks the link afterwards. A source that cannot be read is BLIND, never a failure and never a pass. TWO EXITS, and the difference matters. The doctor SCRIPT exits on what it found: 0 healthy, 1 a link is broken, 2 the registry of agents could not be read, 3 blind. This INTENT exits on whether the door ANSWERED: 0 when it answered, and the doctor's own exit code only when the doctor itself could not run. The verdict is printed as the last line ("verdict: OK|FAIL| BLIND -- ...") and, with json=true, stdout stays a pure JSON document and the verdict line goes to stderr. A doctor's non-zero exit is a FINDING, not a failure of the door: the estate's policy reads an intent's 30-day not-ok rate and refuses a verb at p>=0.8 (platform/estate/bin/estate-execute, policy_decide), so a door that exited on its verdict would be refused exactly when the estate is broken. Measured 2026-10-28: the shadow policy already said "would refuse telegram-agent.doctor -- 5/5 runs not ok in 30d, p_fail=0.86". The executor's own per-intent exit_is_finding flag (docs/specs/2026-09-29-machine-learning-dept.md 6a) is where that belongs estate-wide.
